description: MVP of a data-collection layer that stores only what a camera+IMU rig cannot predict (corollary-discharge cancellation + residual triggering), inspired by Perks et al., Nature 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10690-6).

datasets.description: Rendered rig: static textured scene + gyro-driven camera rotation + injected blob/bar surprise events. The primary benchmark (train/val splits, frames + imu.csv + events.json + featmaps.npy per sequence).
60-second single-scene demo used by the pixel-pipeline experiment (scripts/run_experiment.py).
Webcam field test: real camera, synthetic scene motion, no IMU (sines emulated offline). Used for the webcam readout in README.

Raw Open-AoE segment source (ant-research OpenAoE-2000h via hf-mirror): camera_traj.npz (SLAM cam_c2w), ego_action_annotation.json, undistorted mp4. 9 segments fetched by scripts/fetch_aoe.py (probe 60 -> greedy scene/verb select -> fetch): aoe_20260214_232847_p000 (kitchen/unboxing) + 8 raw_*_seg_* (bathroom, bedroom, childs-room, dining/kitchen/living, workshop, workspace, shop; 134-301 s each).

High-motion Open-AoE pair (top of 259-probed pool by trajectory rotation: p95 |yaw| 51.6/31.0 deg/s; bathroom/hallway/laundry + warehouse/workshop), same layout as data/aoe. Frames deleted after evals (regenerate via prep_aoe.py).

Open-AoE segments converted to the standard sequence layout by scripts/prep_aoe.py: gyro derived from trajectory differentiation (sign auto-calibrated vs DIS flow), per-segment real f_map (10.95-19.17), events = active-manipulation intervals. val/seq_000..seq_011, 12 segments. NOTE: frames/*.png are NOT kept on disk (22 GB lossless stills, regenerable from data/aoe_src videos in ~2 min/segment via prep_aoe.py); only featmaps.npy + imu.csv + events.json persist. Eval scripts error out with a re-prep hint if frames are missing. Also carries features.npy (576-d pooled, streamed from mp4 by scripts/extract_features_aoe.py) and verb_labels.npy (9-class frame-level verbs, scripts/make_verb_labels.py; verbs.json at dataset root) for the real-data downstream value experiment (105-run CV, runs/downstream_aoe_cv.json).

Same high-motion Open-AoE pair rendered at 448px input (f_map doubled to ~38.3, 38x38 featmaps) for the resolution cross-check. Frames are symlinks into prep_aoe output and are deleted after evals alongside data/aoe_motion frames; featmaps/imu/events kept for re-running quality evals (regenerate frames via prep_aoe.py).

10 event-type Open-AoE segments (5 original desktop-level + 5 high-motion, gyro p95 23-75 deg/s, selected by scripts/select_event_segments.py: event-verb filter 3-30% event fraction, motion floor, scene diversity cap) (verbs drop/throw/toss/break; event fraction 3.3-26.3%) prepared by scripts/prep_aoe.py --event-verbs: events.json carries the derived event intervals (note.event_verbs), gyro from trajectory differentiation, featmaps + 576-d pooled features for the sparse-event downstream check (GUIDE 2.3.7). Frames not kept on disk (regenerable from data/aoe_src).

4 walking-level high-motion Open-AoE segments (gyro p95 71-75 deg/s; field/kitchen/balcony/multi-room) prepared by scripts/prep_aoe.py and selected by scripts/select_walk_segments.py (motion floor >= 40 deg/s, scene diversity). Walking-level probe for the gyro-warp value hypothesis (runs/flow_eval_walk.json). Frames not kept on disk (regenerable via prep_aoe.py); featmaps/imu/events persist.

SUPERSEDED by runs/downstream_aoe_cv.json (12-seg 3-fold x 35 seed = 105 runs/method).

results.note: Robust version of the real-data downstream value experiment: 12 Open-AoE segments, 3-fold cross-segment CV x 35 seeds = 105 runs per method, 9 verb classes (fold/grasp/hold/insert/lift/set_down/thread/unfold/wipe) one-vs-rest logistic heads. Rebuilds data/aoe/verbs.json over the 12 segments.
results.headline: NEGATIVE with stats: cerebellum stored 16.0% mAP 0.162+-0.077 ivRec 0.67+-0.12 vs uniform(1x) 0.173+-0.082, oracle (13.2%) 0.164+-0.088 — all mAP within 1 sigma. 'No transfer' is now a statistical conclusion, not a single-split observation.

results.note: Sparse physical event regime check (GUIDE 2.3.7): 10 Open-AoE segments with drop/throw/toss/break verbs (5 original desktop-level + 5 high-motion gyro p95 23-75 deg/s selected by scripts/select_event_segments.py), binary event-frame detection from atomic-action intervals, leave-one-segment-out x 25 seeds = 250 runs per method. 5-segment version was overwritten by this run.
results.headline: NEGATIVE, pinned: cerebellum (23.4% stored) AP 0.108+-0.094 ~= uniform(1x) (23.6%) 0.104+-0.084; oracle (7.9%) best at 0.144+-0.128 but margin shrank vs the 5-seg run (0.204) and evRec no longer leads — kinetic unpredictability as an importance signal is confirmed ineffective on real egocentric data (10 segs, 250 runs, desktop-to-high-motion); the translation-check (runs/trans_eval_data_aoe_event_val.json) closed the escape route: residual noise is world motion (hands), GT translation explains nothing.

results.note: Quality + latency baseline on the 5 event segments (data/aoe_event), robust trigger. Backup of the flow_eval.json output of that run.
results.headline: Event-seg latency baseline: DIS 8.18 ms, gyro shift 0.033 ms, pixel core 0.184 ms, backbone fwd 1.06 ms, full flow step 6.40 ms per frame.

results.note: Event-segment translation check (roadmap item 1): GT camera-frame translation from the AM trajectory is exported in data/aoe_event imu.csv; rotation vs rotation+constant-depth translation warp on featmaps, with frame residual decomposed inside/outside annotated event intervals. No frames needed.
results.headline: NEGATIVE + diagnosis: gyro_trans is worse than gyro on every segment, inside AND outside event intervals (mean calm 0.0679 -> 0.0704); residual inside events ~= outside (0.197 vs 0.193). The event-regime noise is WORLD motion (hands), not egomotion — translation modeling cannot fix 2.3.7, and the flow-arbiter veto experiment (roadmap item 2) is absorbed: flow can only veto camera-motion-explainable candidates, and GT translation already fails to explain the residual.

results.note: Readout-upgrade test (roadmap item 1): same 10-seg LOO x 25 seeds = 250 runs/cell protocol as downstream_event_results, but the downstream input is a spatial readout of the z-map instead of backbone features. Readouts: zamp (1-d global mean of channel-summed z^2), zpyr (21-d log1p spatial pyramid 1+2x2+4x4), feat (576-d baseline), feat+zpyr (concat). Methods: cerebellum / uniform(1x) / oracle.
results.headline: NEGATIVE, decisive: zamp AP is bit-identical across all three storage methods (0.129+-0.098) -- logistic learns zero weights on a signal-free feature and AP collapses to the val event-rate constant; zpyr ~= zamp (spatial pattern adds nothing); feat+zpyr ~= feat (no complementarity); high z-readout evRec (0.84-0.87) is a budget artifact. The z-map carries no event-discriminative information in amplitude OR spatial pattern -- the last value exit inside the motion-prediction framing is closed.

results.note: Walking-level probe (roadmap item 2): 4 high-motion large-scene Open-AoE segments (data/aoe_motion_walk, selected by scripts/select_walk_segments.py, gyro p95 71-75 deg/s: field/kitchen/balcony/multi-room). Quality (robust, calm residual) + latency. Backup of the flow_eval.json output of that run; frames deleted after eval (featmaps/imu/events kept, regenerable).
results.headline: NEGATIVE for gyro value: gyro warp is worse than naive on 3/4 walking-level segs (mean calm 0.1429 -> 0.1582, +11%; per-seq naive/gyro/flow: 0.2105/0.2260/0.1366, 0.1187/0.1445/0.0697, 0.1712/0.1687/0.1320, 0.0713/0.0935/0.0830). DIS flow still wins quality everywhere (mean 0.105, -26% vs naive) at 8.5 ms vs 0.033 ms gyro shift. 'Higher motion -> corollary discharge pays off' FALSIFIED: real-data residual-quality advantage is a synthetic-regime property; walking-level damage is dominated by model-class errors (translation/parallax/rolling shutter) and SLAM-copy degradation.
